column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, loose dump of update 1.1.1). In bring-up: no registered build row, no android.tsv, the host has not
# booted this title yet. RomFS Product.100/Product.111 tables and RegionLangMask.txt "111" put the update at 1.1.1.
# Nintendo EPD's engine (Nin_Ounce: sead / agl / gsys, Phive), an sdk built for the Switch 2 (`spec: Ounce`), NVN2 with Ampere shaders; modules
# main + sdk + subsdk0 (rtld is the SDK's own, as on the other Switch 2 titles). Every RomFS .zs is a zstd frame that names a dictionary from
# Pack/ZsDic.pack.zs (shader_split's zs_dicts), so a reader without that pack sees no asset at all.
# See README.md for the census and docs/SWITCH2.md for what a port needs.

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # ---- Memory (provisional: reservations, none measured on this title yet) ----
# The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on (unlike Donkey Kong Bananza). The first boot asked SetHeapSize for
# 0x18ce00000 (6.22 GB) and the Splatoon Raiders split left only 0x130000000 (4.75 GB), so these are Mario Kart World's reservations, measured on
# this host: 25 GB reserve less 16 GB alias, 256 MB stack and a 256 MB gap leaves 8.5 GB of heap. The reserve is now 34 GB (17.5 GB of heap region) so that
# a heap sized from a 12 GiB total can be granted; like every guest region it is reserved, not committed.
# 12 GiB (0x300000000), the console layout this title plans from — titles size their heap from the reported total. At 9.5 GiB the game asked
# SetHeapSize for 6.66 GB and later died of an uncaught std::bad_alloc with the alias pool only 0.75 GB used; at 48 GiB (a slip: 0xc00000000) it asked
# for 0xb4ce00000 and died when the host refused. The request tracks the reported total, so the number matters.
